idiom_name: makeShape(...): Shape where Shape is a discriminated union + assertNever
implementation_notes: TypeScript types the JavaScript factory function as a function whose return type is a discriminated union over a literal kind tag: a switch then narrows the union, and an exhaustiveness guard (a parameter typed never) turns a forgotten variant into a compile error (typescriptlang.org, Unions and Intersection Types). The factory can return plain objects or class instances, and the union type documents exactly which products exist - something a JavaScript factory cannot express.
pitfalls: The union only narrows while every branch uses a distinct literal tag; widening kind to string silently removes all checking.
assertNever needs strictNullChecks (ideally strict) to work, and the guard must be reached - a missing case that falls through to a default returning undefined compiles without it.
Types are erased at run time: values arriving from JSON, localStorage or a network boundary still need a runtime check before they can be treated as Shape.

variants.name: Abstract class Creator with abstract create()
variants.idiom_name: abstract class Dialog { protected abstract createButton(): Button }
variants.implementation_notes: When products are classes with behaviour and subclassing is part of the design, the classic form stays: an abstract base declares the abstract factory method, subclasses implement it, and TypeScript checks both the override and the product type. TypeScript adds a typing device the classic pattern did not have: an abstract construct signature (new () => Base) lets a constructor itself be injected as the factory while rejecting abstract classes at compile time.
pitfalls: An abstract class cannot be passed where a construct signature (new () => T) is expected; use a concrete subclass or type the parameter as new () => T explicitly.
TypeScript's override and abstract keywords are erased at run time, so nothing stops JavaScript callers from instantiating or mis-implementing the class.
Abstract members with initializers are evaluated in constructor order: a base-class initializer that calls the factory method runs before the subclass override is available.
